title: Fluorescein angiography of the eye
what: A dye is injected into a vein in your arm, and it reaches the blood vessels of your eye in seconds. A camera takes a series of photos of the retina.
why: For diabetes, retina and eye blood vessel conditions, and before laser or eye injections.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes with preparation; the doctor explains the result afterward
tell_doctor: Allergy to dyes, iodine, or any medicine
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
Any past reaction to the dye

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: Your pupils will be widened, so you cannot drive afterward.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your regular medicines on your own.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually have a light meal, unless the clinic says otherwise.

steps: Your pupils are widened with drops
A thin needle or IV line is placed in your arm
You sit at the camera with your chin on a stand
The camera takes many photos with bright flashes
The needle is removed, and you are watched for a short while
feel: A quick prick in the arm
Sometimes nausea for a few seconds after the dye
Your skin may look slightly yellow for a few hours
after: Your urine will be bright yellow for up to 1 to 2 days. That is the dye leaving your body
Drink your usual amount of water
Do not drive until the drops wear off
red_flags: Rash, itching, facial swelling, or trouble breathing: call emergency services
Severe pain or swelling where the needle went in

faq.a: The dye is usually well tolerated. Serious reactions are rare, and help is on hand.
That is the dye leaving your body. It usually clears in 1 to 2 days.

reminders.text: Eye angiography tomorrow. Bring sunglasses and arrange a ride home.
